q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
Q2 FY2027 earnings will be released in approximately 2-3 months (typically in late October 2026, based on standard NVIDIA quarterly reporting schedules). The question asks for the forward guidance provided *in* that earnings release (i.e., guidance for Q3 FY2027), not the Q2 actual results.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

NVIDIA has already provided explicit guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.1B to $92.9B). This was announced on May 20, 2026.

The question asks what guidance will be given *in* the Q2 FY2027 earnings release (scheduled for late October 2026). This would be forward guidance for Q3 FY2027.

To estimate Q3 FY2027 guidance, I need to consider:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion
- Q2 FY2027 expected revenue: $91.0 billion (guidance midpoint)
- This represents ~11.4% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2

**Growth trajectory analysis:**
- If NVIDIA continues strong but more moderate sequential growth in Q3, a reasonable estimate might be 7-12% sequential growth from Q2
- This would place Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance in the range of $97.6B to $102.1B (7-12% growth on $91B)
- Analyst consensus for Q2 is $91.8B, suggesting slight upside to current midpoint guidance

Given NVIDIA's historical pattern of conservative guidance followed by beats, and considering the massive AI/datacenter TAM still being captured, Q3 guidance likely reflects continued strong but potentially moderating growth (10-12% sequential is reasonable).

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Macro slowdown or recession fears dampening AI capex
- Geopolitical restrictions on China exports expanding beyond current constraints
- Data center customers digesting inventory and pulling back orders
- Cryptocurrency market crash reducing demand from mining operations
- Supply chain disruptions for advanced chips
- Competitive pressure from AMD or other alternatives materializing faster than expected

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Accelerating AI adoption beyond current expectations
- Surprise demand from new applications (robotics, autonomous vehicles)
- Major cloud provider announcements of expanded AI infrastructure spending
- Geopolitical tensions reducing China competition concerns
- Margin expansion allowing higher revenue targets at same profitability
- Better-than-expected execution on new product launches

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue: $81.6B (up 85% YoY)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ± 2% (midpoint)
- Sequential growth Q1→Q2: 11.4%

The guidance range provided ($99.5B to $115.5B) spans $99.5B to $115.5B, with the center at approximately $107.5B. This represents roughly 18% sequential growth from the Q2 guidance midpoint ($91.0B), which would be unusually aggressive unless demand accelerates significantly.

However, historical NVIDIA patterns show:
- Consistent sequential growth during bull markets
- Conservative guidance that gets beaten
- Recent quarterly growth rates in the 10-12% range seem sustainable but acceleration to 18%+ appears optimistic

**My estimate:**
The most likely Q3 FY2027 guidance range would be approximately $100-108B, reflecting 10-18.5% sequential growth from Q2. Given NVIDIA's pattern of conservative guidance and the strength of the AI cycle, I'll estimate toward the higher end of a reasonable growth scenario but not the absolute maximum in the provided range.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA announced on May 20, 2026, its outlook for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, projecting revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA also anticipates GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins of 74.9% and 75.0% respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points, and GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $8.5 billion and $8.3 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). Analysts have a consensus revenue estimate for Q2 FY2027 of $91.8 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, up 85% year-over-year [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).
